judge: mockup-craft-reviewer (Opus), blind to the HTML — graded on rendered full-page PNGs only

directions.name: the-lit-clearing-3-2
directions.concept: THE CENTRED APERTURE — every clearing centred on the page axis, growing symmetrically outward, each plate mounted in a near-black mat that narrows as the light grows.
directions.faceClearance: PASS (measured, round 3) — portrait x 1001-1375, clearing x 65-958, 43px gap. Took THREE attempts: a box across her nose and cheeks, then a horizontal band across the same, then finally the two-frame restructure.
directions.gradeIsStale: Graded BEFORE repair. Two disqualifying defects at grade time: a blush box lying across her nose and cheeks, and 'Restructuring.' overflowing the clearing's right edge onto the photograph one beat after the hero promises 'Nothing crosses this edge.' Both fixed; hero re-based 288->619px so the three key sentences set on three lines. Needs re-grading.
directions.oneLineReason: Distinctive and genuinely place-made, but it repeated the rejected sin — a blush box straight across Marianne's nose and cheeks — and broke its own stated invariant when type overflowed the clearing's edge onto the photograph.

directions.name: the-lit-clearing-3-5
directions.concept: THE ROOM DECIDES — the photograph is chosen and cropped first, and the clearing is placed wherever the room actually left space.
directions.faceClearance: FAIL at grade time (measured + 1:1 crop) — clearing hid her right eye; corner within 25-90px of the near eye. Two-frame restructure dispatched.
directions.oneLineReason: Beats 1-4 are genuinely good and emotionally right — a real woman in a real room — but three of the six operator rejections recur, and the schedule dumps ~40 elements and nine dark photo plates INSIDE the second-widest clearing.

directions.name: the-lit-clearing-3-4
directions.concept: SPOKEN FROM THE LIGHT, SPOKEN FROM THE ROOM — strict alternation between beats whose words sit inside the clearing and beats whose words are set on the plate at display scale.
directions.faceClearance: PASS (measured + 1:1 crop) — both eyes, nose, mouth and chin intact; the clearing's left edge lands on hair past her cheek. The only variant to pass without needing the two-frame restructure.
directions.gradeIsStale: Graded BEFORE repair. At grade time the page had NO booking action at all — its Crown was a headline over ~800px of inert near-black on a page whose nav says 'Ask for an hour'. Booking action restored; three-up grid replaced with a hairline ledger; two designer-voice plate captions cut. Needs re-grading.
directions.oneLineReason: The top half is genuinely strong — alternating clearings and plates, a warm human world, the three plain promises in the first viewport — but the bottom half collapsed into a three-up card grid and a Crown with no way to book.

directions.name: the-lit-clearing-3-1
directions.concept: THE SWINGING WEDGE — the clearing grows while its anchor alternates left/right down the page, so the wedge swings as it widens.

supersededGrade.note: graded before the repair pass AND before the operator-directed edit sequence (inter-section bars removed, schedule rebuilt as a full-width three-column ledger, portrait moved into a circle inside the what-this-is-not clearing, closing altar section added, footer inverted to white)

directions.oneLineReason: A concept-derived alternating-plate composition with real human warmth — held off a 9 only by the three-panel schedule reading closest to a card row, its micro-type, and a footer whose white text fights a busy floral photograph.
openDefects: Schedule ledger rows set well below the rest of the page type floor.
Footer white text over a busy floral photograph costs legibility at the last impression.
The centred Everything-runs-here heading floats over an incidental window photograph doing no work.

directions.name: the-lit-clearing-3-3
directions.concept: THE PLATE SEQUENCE — every beat is a discrete framed plate, separated by bands of near-black carrying one line each; the bands narrow as the clearing widens.
directions.faceClearance: PASS (measured) — portrait in its own frame, clearing beside it, zero overlap. The first variant in the family to achieve genuine clearance, and the template the others copied.
directions.gradeIsStale: Graded BEFORE repair. The 5/10 was driven mainly by the face-bisection which has since been fixed structurally, plus caption-tax, flat separator bands, the beat-7 density inversion and a teal photograph out of the colour world — all four also addressed. Needs re-grading.
directions.oneLineReason: The plate sequence and its monotonic growth genuinely work and the hero answers the undress/touch/believe question in plain sentences — but F-3 recurred in a worse form: the blush plate was a vertical guillotine through the middle of Marianne's face.

directions.name: the-lit-clearing-5
directions.concept: THE HAND AT THE EDGE — every clearing cropped so Marianne's hand meets the boundary of the light and stops, at a different scale and direction each beat, inverted exactly once at the close.
directions.exceptionReason: Sub-threshold and NOT regenerated — recorded honestly. The premise is sound and the schedule is strong; the failure is a cropping-craft problem that a targeted pass could fix.
directions.oneLineReason: Distinctive, warm and correctly human for the category, but the variant's entire premise fails: only one beat in eight actually shows a hand arriving at a clearing's boundary and stopping, while the hero copy explicitly promises it at every beat.
directions.signatureMoveVerified: BROKEN. 1 of 8 beats genuinely lands the motif (and against a non-clearing), 1 partial, 6 absent, and 1 ACTIVELY CONTRADICTS it — at the four-verb beat the same forearm appears above AND below the clearing, reading unambiguously as the arm passing behind the light.
directions.cardCheck: PASS — 'the best thing on the page'. Genuinely rows in a continuous field of light: no per-item background, border, radius or shadow, picture beside text rather than stacked on it, one unbroken pale field. The card failure has not recurred.
openHandFixes: P1 re-crop every beat around the BOUNDARY rather than around the subject — clearings are currently placed for text layout with whatever photograph fell behind them.
P2 kill the four-verb crossing — the arm must not appear on both sides of that clearing; it contradicts the page's central claim.
P3 three dead regions: an empty pale rectangle, a flat maroon block, and a near-black illegible band.
P4 the closing inversion is only half-delivered — the promised empty chair with the coat is not legible.
P5 bring 'What this is not' into a clearing in plum ink — currently the hardest-to-read paragraph and the one most likely to decide a booking.
P6 schedule thumbnails are postage-stamp sized and several are an indistinct dark blur.

directions.name: the-lit-clearing-3
directions.concept: THE WIDENING APERTURE — the clearing starts the size of a seated person and grows monotonically at every beat until it consumes the viewport, while the element count runs the opposite way.
directions.exceptionReason: Sub-threshold and NOT regenerated — recorded honestly rather than silently passed. Its single signature move is measurably broken and the fixes are specific enough for a targeted pass whenever the operator wants it.
directions.oneLineReason: The widening wedge — this variant's only signature move — breaks twice in the middle third: beat 4 is measurably NARROWER than beat 3, beat 5 abandons the clearing entirely leaving a blank pale slab, and the widest clearing carries by far the MOST elements, the exact inversion failure the brief named.
directions.signatureMoveVerified: BROKEN. Widths measured: 227 / 360 / 456 / 414 (REVERSES -42px) / [beat 5 exits the mechanism] / 671 / 761 / 831. Not monotonic.
directions.cardCheck: PARTIAL — no per-item background, border, shadow or radius, and all three groups sit in one continuous pale field, so the photographs genuinely are dark rectangles cut into light. But the arrangement is a strict 3-up grid repeated three times with identical stacks and identically-sized apertures — the catalogue shape the direction bans outright.
openHandFixes: P1 kill the beat-4 reversal — widen it past beat 3's right edge. Non-negotiable; it is the whole variant.
P2 beat 5 renders an empty pale slab while the trust-critical 'Not therapy / Not medicine' copy sits at ~13px pale on a photograph — the least legible thing on the page at the most anxious moment.
P3 break the schedule's 3-up grid rhythm — vary aperture sizes so the dark shapes read as cut rather than tiled.
P4 cut the schedule's element count; drop the redundant COURSE/WORKSHOP/SERVICE eyebrows and pull the date onto its own line.
P5 size up the hero statement — the cramp should come from the box, not from timid type.
P6 the footer is a completely flat pale field with no photograph.
P7 raise body copy from 13px page-wide.

directions.name: the-lit-clearing-1
directions.concept: THE LEDGER BAND — the clearing is a full-width horizontal ribbon of light with photograph above and below it; band height varies per beat and that variation is the rhythm. The schedule is one continuous ledger per offering kind.
directions.oneLineReason: The ledger band genuinely holds for two-thirds of the page — varying band heights, marginal group labels, contained hairlines, last item cut by the viewport — but the CTA band is half-empty and the schedule photographs are inset thumbnails floating in the light rather than holes cut through it.
directions.cardCheck: PARTIAL — no card grammar (no stroke, shadow, radius, elevation or tinted panel; blush runs edge to edge; hairlines stop cleanly inside the band; the 4th item bleeds off the right edge in all three bands). BUT every photograph is inset ~18px of blush on all four sides, so it reads as a picture placed on a background rather than a hole cut through. Close the gutter and the concept snaps.
openHandFixes: P1 kill the ~18px photo inset in all three schedule bands so the plate reads as showing THROUGH the band — this is the concept-or-not fix.
P2 the CTA band is correctly the tallest but ~55% empty blush, tripping the no-flat-pale-region invariant; resolve the ledger rather than abandon it.
P3 an empty full-width blush band in tile 4 containing nothing reads as a layout fault.
P4 suspected clipped row of glyphs sitting on a band's bottom edge in the Heart beat — type must never cross a clearing boundary; verify and clear.
P5 schedule item body copy too small for a 35-65 reader while carrying the load-bearing commerce detail.
P6 'WHAT THIS IS NOT' sets cream body over a photograph — the witty rule-break is worth keeping but the yellow eyebrow is hard to read.
P7 top nav is small cream type over the brightest part of the hero photograph.

directions.name: the-lit-clearing-2
directions.concept: THE MIGRATING COLUMN — a tall narrow column of light steps across the page as the scroll descends, flush left at the first beat to flush right at the last; the schedule becomes her diary.
directions.oneLineReason: The migrating column and the diary-as-one-column-of-light both land — genuinely distinctive, warm and human — but the 'What this is not' beat leaves an EMPTY clearing while its copy is orphaned onto the dark photograph at the far left, reading as a reversal of the migration.
directions.signatureMoveVerified: Migration measured beat by beat: 0 / 83 / 165 / 247 / [broken] / 400 / 410 / 656 — a clean ~82px-per-beat descent with correct endpoints, but beat 5 snaps back to the far left and beats 6-7 repeat position (400 vs 410) while the diary dwells for 3000px.
directions.cardCheck: PASS, decisively — 'the best thing on the page'. One unbroken pale field, entries separated only by hairline rules, date rotated 90 degrees as a plum spine, aperture flush at the column's right edge. No rectangle, shadow, radius, or picture-stacked-on-text.
openHandFixes: P1 beat 5 renders an empty white clearing while its copy sits on the dark photograph at the far left — breaks the migration AND two base invariants at once.
P2 beats 6 and 7 share a horizontal position; push the diary right to ~490 so the staircase keeps ticking.
P3 body copy ~2px too small throughout for a 35-65 audience.
P4 several diary hairlines run to the clearing's right boundary — nothing may touch the edge; stop them at the aperture.
P5 empty pale tail strip below the last diary entry.
P6 the footer is the page's one flat pale full-bleed slab with a template-ish 3-column link grid.
P7 hero line 1 wraps leaving 'on.' alone on its own line.

directions.name: the-lit-clearing-4
directions.concept: THE SPLIT PLATE — the page divides down its whole length into a photographic column and a continuous reading column of light, side by side; the unbroken vertical seam is the signature, and it breaks exactly once at the CTA.
directions.oneLineReason: The split plate is genuinely delivered — one constant seam at ~62/38 held for the whole scroll, a hairline ledger schedule with apertures flush to the seam (no cards), zero type on the photographic side, and a named single break at the CTA — but the photographic column goes nearly imageless for ~600px in the Workshops stretch and the 'doorway opens' payoff is a thin murky letterbox strip.
directions.signatureMoveVerified: Seam measured at x=533 on every tile from the top edge through to the break — no drift, no inset, no proportion change. Constant 62/38, deliberate rather than half-and-half.
directions.cardCheck: PASS — rows, unambiguously. Hairline rules, date eyebrow left, price right-aligned, aperture flush to the seam. No self-contained rectangles, no picture-stacked-on-text, no backgrounds, no shadows.
openHandFixes: P1 ~600px of the photographic column carries a featureless dark maroon blur behind the Workshops beat — a flat region where the direction requires a photograph.
P2 the once-only seam break is a ~50px tonally dead letterbox strip, and a second dark band above the footer makes the break read twice.
P3 the CTA control is a plain filled magenta rectangle — the one template artefact in the composition.
P4 schedule apertures are ~100px slivers; several are indistinguishable from one another, so 'a picture on every item' is met only thinly.
P5 Services aperture strip is continuous where Courses/Workshops have inter-row gaps — row-to-aperture correspondence goes vague.
P6 body and schedule-description type ~10% too small for a 35-65 audience.
P7 row hairlines stop ~20px short of the aperture so each aperture floats unattached to its row.
P8 photographic-side image changes land mid-paragraph rather than on beat boundaries.

directions.name: the-lit-clearing-v2
directions.oneLineReason: A genuinely distinctive near-black photographic scroll with cream pools of light carrying real human presence and plain reassuring copy; held back by a schedule region that multiplies the clearing into three rows of opaque cream tiles with sliver-sized pictures, and by body type set too small for a 35-65 audience.
regenHistory: r0 5/10 FAIL — operator-requested schedule carousel shipped as a 3x3 grid of image-cards on flat white, the archetype's explicit EXCLUDE.

r1 6/10 pass — schedule inverted correctly (clearings burned out of one continuous plate) but the agent satisfied it by AMPUTATING the operator-required per-item photographs; deleting the 'Not therapy' orphan block also deleted its clearing, leaving low-contrast ink on a bare plate.

r2 ungraded — reviewer correctly REFUSED to grade rather than fabricate: the 1440x9426 single-strip PNG exceeded its read path and loop-detection latched. Render is now tiled into 8 viewport slices (_t2-01..08) for review; per-viewport is also the correct unit of judgement for a one-clearing-per-viewport archetype.

r3 7/10 pass — aperture/clearing proportions had been built inverted (440px photo vs 120px text ribbon, ~1.5 items per row, so it did not read as a carousel) and every item in a row reused one re-cropped photograph. Swapped to narrow aperture + wide clearing, distinct photograph per item, row height reduced to show ~2.5 items with the third clipped. Row labels had been near-black on a near-black plate — root cause was a missing background on .row-label-clearing.
directions.exceptionReason: ACCEPTED ABOVE THRESHOLD, BUT THE feat-106 REGEN CAP (2) WAS EXCEEDED — 3 regenerations ran. Recorded rather than hidden. The third was not a craft-score chase: r1 and r2 both failed to deliver the OPERATOR's explicit requirement (a browsable carousel row per offering kind, every item carrying a picture), and the fix was a width/asset change rather than a redesign. If the cap is meant to bind on operator-requirement fixes as well as craft-score fixes, that is a policy gap worth closing explicitly rather than by silent overrun.
openHandFixes: P1 body copy ~13-14px across several prose blocks; brief's audience skews 35-65 and asks to assume reading glasses are elsewhere. Take body to 17-18px.
P2 11px magenta micro-caps eyebrows with heavy tracking are the least legible type on the page.
P3 nav links ~13px at low contrast directly on a dark photographic plate.
P4 schedule item pictures are a ~78px sliver against a ~235px panel; widen toward 40% of item width and re-crop so the subject reads at thumbnail scale (Services crops carry no information).
P5 no carousel affordance beyond the edge clip — no arrow, dot or counter; a 60-year-old may not know the rows move.

P6 schedule still multiplies clearings per viewport (label chip + 3 items), diluting one-clearing-per-viewport; the reviewer's cheapest honest fix is ONE continuous cream band per row with pictures cut into it as apertures and hairline rules between items.
P7 workshops row image strips overhang the panel by ~6-8px inconsistently across rows.
P8 right-edge clip lands mid-word on all three rows.
directions.provenanceNote: This 7/10 grade belongs to the VARIATION, not the original. The original the-lit-clearing was overwritten in place during this work (operator had asked for new variations FROM it, not edits TO it); it was recovered from the ui-designer agent transcript and restored to docs/mockups/the-lit-clearing/webapp/home.html. The original is UNGRADED in this ledger — its earlier grade predates 2026-08-08.

directions.name: the-answer-printed-first
directions.oneLineReason: Print-editorial front page; bravest opening screen. Docked: one four-up grid reversion, and the register is prosecutorial where the brief asks warm.

directions.name: no-seam-nightfield
directions.oneLineReason: Answers the sceptic as a labelled contract (OWN CLOTHES / NO CONTACT / NOT REQUIRED) and its CTA is her actual diary. Docked: chakra ladder as spine on a page promising no beliefs required.

directions.name: the-room-you-are-standing-in
directions.oneLineReason: Best signature move in the set (the four-verb staircase) but ships a visible bracketed TODO in the practitioner beat and several plum-on-plum near-unreadable paragraphs.

directions.name: the-refusal-column
directions.oneLineReason: 'I do not diagnose / I look' antiphony is the finest device in the set; cold BY DESIGN and well made, but earns trust without ever lifting anyone — the client's own success test goes unmet.

directions.name: long-dusk-ascent
directions.oneLineReason: Real structural ascent across 9000px, but the gradient goes muddy grey-mauve exactly at 'What this is not', that beat is three lines in a dead field, and form inputs read as disabled.

directions.name: the-mark-is-the-grid
directions.oneLineReason: Warmest page; 'THE ONE STRAIGHT EDGE ON THIS PAGE' is a signature worth the territory. Unresolved: staircase jams the right edge, near-empty circle, pricing alignments never meet.

directions.name: fixed-band-editable-field
directions.exceptionReason: PENDING REGENERATION. The stagger never resolves (wandering right margin), the fixed band has two long dead stretches, AND it prints internal pipeline vocabulary ('BEAT TWO — THE HOUR, FROM THE INSIDE') plus inline '[Practitioner name — to confirm]' brackets on the client's homepage. Its own author diagnosed the dead-field defect but hit its turn ceiling before fixing it.

directions.name: one-lamp-amber
directions.exceptionReason: PENDING REGENERATION. The category skeleton in the dark — hero→mission→four stacked services→photo→testimonial→disclaimer→prices→CTA. A huge blank near-black rectangle after 'This is not therapy' reads as a failed render; brown-on-brown 'before and after' band effectively illegible. NOTE: this was the ONLY agent to complete its self-verification and report every check green — the strongest possible argument for judging pixels over self-reports.

directions.name: plate-sequence-captioned
directions.exceptionReason: PENDING REGENERATION. Category cliché in editorial dress — plates decorate a template rather than deriving from an idea. PLATE 05 is a formless orange blur that reads as a broken image. Whole page set lowercase in small low-contrast grey, so the one sentence that matters is demoted to near-body size. Also self-defeating: it opens by mocking sites made of atmospheric photographs, then is one.

systemicFindings: VISIBLE PLACEHOLDER LEAK (4 of 10: the-room-you-are-standing-in, the-refusal-column, the-mark-is-the-grid, fixed-band-editable-field). Caused by the PARENT's own dispatch preamble, which said 'Write around them or use a visibly marked placeholder' for the unverified practitioner name. The second half of that instruction produced comps that cannot be shown to the paying client. Fix the instruction, not the ten mockups.

INTERNAL VOCABULARY LEAK (fixed-band-editable-field printed 'BEAT TWO', 'BEAT THREE', 'BEAT FIVE' as section labels). The brief's §11 beat table is pipeline scaffolding, not client-facing copy; the dispatch never said so.

UNDER-DESIGNED NEGATIVE SPACE + UNDERSIZED TYPE (8 of 10). 'dead dusk field', 'large void to its right', 'huge blank dark rectangle', 'near-empty circle', 'two long dead stretches', 'plum-on-plum close to unreadable', 'pale-on-pale looking disabled', '9-10px marginalia'. Nine of ten agents hit their turn ceiling DURING the render-and-look pass that catches exactly this class.

THE LOOK-AND-REFINE STEP NEEDS ITS OWN BUDGET. 9 of 10 ui-designer dispatches were truncated mid-verification or mid-fix, several having already correctly diagnosed their own defect. The step that produces quality is the last to run and the first to be cut.
summary.winnerGrade: the-lit-clearing-3-1 = 8 (pass), re-graded 2026-08-08 after repair + operator edits; prior 5/fail was stale
